newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Sons Gwalia completes hedge restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Sons Gwalia completes hedge restructuring.

text.p: Gold miner Sons of Gwalia Ltd said on Monday that it had completed the restructuring of its hedge book annnounced on Friday.

The company said the restructure, which raised A$60 million, was achieved by the closing out of 295,000 ounces of put options that were surplus to its revised gold production profile, and by reducing the strike price on the remaining 2.39 million put options held by the company.
The average strike price of the remaining put options was reduced to A$610 from A$638, the company said.
As a result of the restructuring, the company said its hedge book now totalled 4.56 million ounces for delivery from 1997/98 to 2006/2007 at an average price of A$629 per ounce.
However, all gold production for the 1997/98 financial year would be sold at no less than A$660 per ounce, the company said.

The current hedge book consisted of 2.39 million ounces of put options at an average strike price of A$610 per ounce, 800,000 ounces of convertible put options exercisable between 2000/01 to 2000/07 at an average strike price of A$655 per ounce, and 1.37 million ounces of forward sales contracts at an average sale price of A$648 per ounce.

On Friday, the company announced a net loss for the 12 months to June 30 of A$128.39 million after an abnormal loss of A$167.78 million from a writedown of exporation interests and the carrying value of its operating mining assets.
At 12.15 p.m. (0215 GMT), Sons of Gwalia shares were five cents lower at A$4.85 on minimal turnover of 9,144 shares.
